title: Run-Length Compress
statement:
**Run-length encoding** replaces every run of the same letter by the letter followed by the length of the run. For example `aaabcc` becomes `a3b1c2` (a run of length 1 is still written, as `b1`).

Return the run-length encoding of `text`.
constraints: text contains only lowercase letters a-z

examples.explanation: Three a's, one b, two c's.
A single letter is a run of length 1.

hints.nudge: Walk through the text. When does a run end?
hints.pattern: Two pointers (or a counter) scanning runs, building the result in a list.
hints.pseudocode:
result = []; i = 0
while i < n:
  j = i
  while j < n and text[j] == text[i]: j++
  result.append(text[i] + str(j - i))
  i = j
return join(result)
hints.walkthrough: Start at the first letter and extend j while the letters are equal; the run length is j - i. Append the letter and the length, then continue from j. Every character is visited once, so O(n). Build the answer with a list or string builder instead of repeated string concatenation, which can be O(n^2) in some languages. Remember the count can have several digits (for example a12).
